title: 1775: the Patriots take the forts
text: The royal government loses its grip. Patriot leaders carry off the arms in Charleston in April, and the Crown's forts at Fort Charlotte (July) and Fort Johnson (September) are taken without a fight. In November Loyalists besiege Williamson's camp at Ninety Six for two days until a truce ends it; in December the Patriots break the Loyalist camp at Great Cane Brake and the Snow Campaign scatters the rest.

title: 1776: the fort holds, the Cherokee war
text: In June the palmetto fort on Sullivan's Island drives off the British fleet, and Breach Inlet stops the landing. From July the Cherokee strike the frontier. Williamson's column is ambushed at Esseneca on 1 August, the one Cherokee win drawn here, then beats a war party on 12 August and burns the Lower Towns; Fort Rutledge is built at Esseneca.

title: 1777: a gap in the list
text: The Archives list has no action for 1777. The one thing read for the year is the end of the Cherokee war: the treaty of 20 May 1777 gives up the Lower Towns' lands.

title: 1778: one entry
text: The list has one entry for the year, the capture of privateers at Charleston on 19 Jun. Nothing read says who took them.

title: 1779: the war comes south
text: Moultrie beats Gardiner's detachment on Port Royal Island in February. In May Prevost reaches the Charleston lines and draws off when Lincoln hurries back. On 20 June Lincoln's attack on the rear guard at Stono Ferry is repulsed, and the British fall back to Beaufort.

title: 1780: Charleston falls, then the partisan war
text: Clinton lands in February, crosses the Ashley on 29 March, and Lincoln surrenders the city and army on 12 May. Tarleton wins at Monck's Corner, Lenud's Ferry and the Waxhaws, and British posts run inland to Camden, Ninety Six and the Cheraws. The partisans answer: Huck's Defeat, Rocky Mount and Hanging Rock, Sumter's raid at Wateree Ferry, Musgrove Mill and Marion's raids. Gates is routed at Camden on 16 August and Sumter at Fishing Creek two days later. Kings Mountain in October turns the tide; Blackstock's, Rugeley's and Hammond's Store follow.

title: 1781: Cowpens
text: Greene's army rests at the Cheraws, and Morgan's detachment works west of the Broad. On 17 January Morgan beats Tarleton at Cowpens. The playback ends here; the later actions are loaded as data for a second stage.

title: Where things stood on 17 January 1781
text: The British hold Charleston and its harbour forts, Beaufort, Georgetown, Dorchester, Monck's Corner, Orangeburg, Fort Granby, Fort Galphin, Camden, Ninety Six and Cornwallis's camp at Winnsboro. Greene's army holds the Cheraws. Fort Charlotte, Esseneca, Tamassee and Kingstree are drawn as contested: no source read puts them under either side after June 1780. Who held what is reconstructed from the sources named on each place, not from a survey of the time, and several posts are dated only to the month.
